# Go live

> Publish live audio to a stored transcription, and put it on a broadcast link listeners open. Control is HTTP; audio is one WebSocket.

| Endpoint | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/transcriptions/live` | Create a live transcription |
| `POST /v1/broadcasts` | Create a broadcast |
| `PUT /v1/transcriptions/{id}/broadcasts/{broadcast}` | Attach a broadcast |
| `POST /v1/transcriptions/{id}/recordings` | Start a recording |
| `POST /v1/recordings/{id}/pause` | Pause a recording |
| `POST /v1/recordings/{id}/resume` | Resume a recording |
| `POST /v1/recordings/{id}/stop` | Stop a recording |
| `WS /v1/realtime/sessions/{token}/socket` | Connect to the `streamUrl` a realtime session returned (treat it as opaque). |

A realtime session is gone when its socket closes. To keep what is said, and let other people follow it as it happens, publish to a **live transcription**: it is stored as it is spoken, listed under Transcriptions, and its recordings can be read, translated, exported and shared afterwards. A **broadcast** is the link listeners open (`code`, `shareUrl`); it is fed by the live transcriptions attached to it. The order: create the live transcription, optionally put it on a broadcast, start a recording, publish audio to its `streamUrl`, and control it over HTTP.

## 1. Create a live transcription

`POST /v1/transcriptions/live` with a `name` and optional `settings` (`spokenLanguage`, `speakerLabels`, `latencyMode`…) creates it idle. Nothing is recorded until a recording starts. Its `source` can also be a stream the server pulls itself (a YouTube live, an internet radio address), in which case there is no audio for you to send.

## 2. Put it on a broadcast

`POST /v1/broadcasts` creates the link (`code`, and `shareUrl` to hand out; `access: "private"` and a `password` keep it to the people you give them). `PUT /v1/transcriptions/{id}/broadcasts/{broadcast}` feeds it from the live transcription. One transcription can feed several broadcasts and a broadcast several transcriptions. Listeners follow it with the subscribe socket ([Listen](listen.md)).

## 3. Start a recording

`POST /v1/transcriptions/{id}/recordings` starts one and answers with a publish grant: `recording` (its `id` is what you control and read it by), `sessionId` and `streamUrl`. A `409 conflict` with `details.takeover` means another device is recording it now; repeat with `{ "takeover": true }` to record from here instead.

## 4. Publish audio

Connect to `streamUrl` and publish exactly as on a realtime session ([Stream a microphone](stream-a-microphone.md)): wait for `session.ready`, send raw PCM (`pcm_f32le`, 16 kHz, mono) as binary frames, and read commits back. The difference is that every commit is also stored and fanned out to the recording's subscribers, translated into the languages they read. A cold machine can take a minute to become ready: give `connect` a long ready deadline (`readyDeadlineMs`, `ready_deadline_s`, PHP's `readyDeadline:` in seconds).

## 5. Pause, resume and stop

Control is HTTP, never a frame on the socket: `pause` (idempotent), `resume`, and `stop`, which is allowed only from paused. Sending `eof` on the publisher socket also ends the recording. A recording moves `live` ⇄ `paused` → `ended` → `finalized` (its transcript settled); listeners stay connected through `ended`. A recording left paused longer than `settings.maxPauseS` ends by itself.

## Complete code

Each program runs as it is once `VOCALSTACK_API_KEY` holds one of your API keys.

### `live.ts`

```typescript
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { VocalStack } from '@vocalstack/sdk';

const vs = new VocalStack({ baseUrl: 'https://api.vocalstack.com', apiKey: process.env.VOCALSTACK_API_KEY });

const tx = await vs.transcriptions.createLive({ name: 'Town hall', settings: { spokenLanguage: 'en' } });

const broadcast = await vs.broadcasts.create({ name: 'Town hall' });
await vs.transcriptions.attachBroadcast(tx.id, broadcast.id);
console.log('listeners open', broadcast.shareUrl);

const grant = await vs.transcriptions.startRecording(tx.id);
const recordingId = grant.recording.id;

const stream = await vs.recordings.publish(grant, { readyDeadlineMs: 180_000 }); // a cold machine can take a while
// -re reads the file at its own pace, as a microphone would arrive. For a
// microphone: -f avfoundation -i :0 (macOS), -f pulse -i default (Linux).
const ffmpeg = spawn('ffmpeg', ['-loglevel', 'error', '-re', '-i', './talk.mp3', '-f', 'f32le', '-ac', '1', '-ar', '16000', '-']);
ffmpeg.stdout.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => stream.sendAudio(new Uint8Array(chunk)));

// eof ends the recording when the audio does; pause, resume and stop are HTTP.
ffmpeg.on('close', () => stream.eof());
process.once('SIGINT', async () => {
  ffmpeg.kill();
  await vs.recordings.pause(recordingId);
  await vs.recordings.stop(recordingId); // only from paused
});

for await (const ev of stream) {
  if (ev.type === 'transcript.committed') console.log(`#${ev.segment.seq} ${ev.segment.text}`);
}

console.log('ended:', (await vs.recordings.get(recordingId)).state);
```
